answers.label: Q2
answers.finalAnswer: \(\frac{17}{24}\); \(\frac{35}{48}\) (any two such as \(\frac{49}{72}, \frac{25}{36}\) are also correct)
answers.solution:
Mean of the two numbers: \(\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2}{3} + \frac{3}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{17}{12} = \frac{17}{24}\)
So \(\frac{2}{3} < \frac{17}{24} < \frac{3}{4}\) (that is, \(\frac{16}{24} < \frac{17}{24} < \frac{18}{24}\)).
Mean of \(\frac{17}{24}\) and \(\frac{3}{4}\): \(\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{17}{24} + \frac{18}{24}\right) = \frac{35}{48}\)
So \(\frac{17}{24} < \frac{35}{48} < \frac{3}{4}\).
(Another way: \(\frac{2}{3} = \frac{48}{72}\), \(\frac{3}{4} = \frac{54}{72}\), so \(\frac{49}{72}, \frac{50}{72}, \ldots, \frac{53}{72}\) all lie between them.)

So, two rational numbers between \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(\frac{3}{4}\) are \(\frac{17}{24}\) and \(\frac{35}{48}\).

So, A = 8, B = 6, C = 4, D = 4, E = 5, F = 6, G = 3, H = 6, and the division is \(486 \div 9 = 54\).

Long division:
\(x^3 \div x^2 = x\); \(x(x^2 - 4x + 3) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x\)
Subtract: \((x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x) - (x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x) = -2x^2 + 8x\); bring down \(-6\): \(-2x^2 + 8x - 6\)
\(-2x^2 \div x^2 = -2\); \(-2(x^2 - 4x + 3) = -2x^2 + 8x - 6\)
Subtract: remainder 0
Check: \((x^2 - 4x + 3)(x - 2) = (x - 1)(x - 3)(x - 2) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6\).

So, the quotient is \(x - 2\) and the remainder is 0.

In triangle ABC, \(\angle A = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle C = 30^\circ\), so \(\angle B = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ\).
x, y and z are the exterior angles at A, B and C (each on a straight line with the interior angle):
\(x = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\)
\(y = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\)
\(z = 180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ\)
\(x + y + z = 90^\circ + 120^\circ + 150^\circ = 360^\circ\)
(This agrees with the rule that the exterior angles of a triangle add up to \(360^\circ\).)

So, \(x + y + z = 360^\circ\).

Four equal circles touch each other in pairs inside the 14 cm square, so each has diameter 7 cm and radius \(\frac{7}{2}\) cm.

Area of one circle \(= \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{7}{2} \times \frac{7}{2} = 38.5\) cm²
Area of four circles \(= 4 \times 38.5 = 154\) cm²
Area of the square enclosed between the circles \(= 196 - 154 = 42\) cm²
(With the textbook version, circles of radius 7 cm centred at the corners, the four quarter-circles also make 154 cm² and the space they enclose is again 42 cm².)

So, the area of the part of the square enclosed between the circles is 42 cm² (the circles themselves cover 154 cm²).

answers.label: Q22
answers.finalAnswer: Triangle with AB = 6 cm, ∠B = 60°, ∠A = 45°; AC ≈ 5.4 cm; BC ≈ 4.4 cm
answers.solution:
As printed the question names \(\angle CBA\) twice (\(60^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\)), which is impossible. The sensible reading is \(\angle CBA = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle CAB = 45^\circ\); then \(\angle ACB = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 45^\circ = 75^\circ\).
Steps of construction:
1. Draw AB = 6 cm with a ruler.
2. At B, construct \(60^\circ\): with centre B draw an arc cutting BA at P; with centre P and the same radius cut this arc at Q. Join BQ and produce it.
3. At A, construct \(90^\circ\) (mark two \(60^\circ\) arcs and bisect the second \(60^\circ\)), then bisect the \(90^\circ\) angle to get \(45^\circ\). Draw this ray.
4. The two rays meet at C. ABC is the required triangle.
Measure: \(AC \approx 5.4\) cm and \(BC \approx 4.4\) cm.
(Check by calculation: \(AC = \frac{6 \sin 60^\circ}{\sin 75^\circ} \approx 5.38\) cm, \(BC = \frac{6 \sin 45^\circ}{\sin 75^\circ} \approx 4.39\) cm. If instead \(\angle A = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle B = 45^\circ\), the two lengths swap: AC ≈ 4.4 cm, BC ≈ 5.4 cm.)

So, AC is about 5.4 cm and BC is about 4.4 cm.
